external.label: Bulk silica and mineral proportions — USGS
external.citation: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, Components of Igneous Rocks
external.supports: An illustrative granite composition distinguishes bulk SiO₂ from mineral proportions. It is not an Egyptian sample.

external.label: Giza stone supply — Mark Lehner
external.citation: Mark Lehner, The Treasures of the Pyramids, pp. 32–45
external.supports: Archaeological description of local core limestone, imported fine casing limestone and Aswan granite. Supply description is not a specimen assay.

external.label: Pyramid petrography — Campbell and Folk, 1991
external.citation: D. H. Campbell and R. L. Folk, Ancient Egyptian Pyramids—Concrete or Rock, Concrete International 13(8), 28, 30–39 (1991)
external.supports: Reports geological fabrics and absence of proposed geopolymer fabric in examined material. Preserve sample scope.
external.access: Publisher abstract; full paper not inspected

external.label: Granite and molten carbonate — Yi, 2026
external.citation: Xiang Yi, npj Heritage Science 14, 51 (2026), published 22 January 2026
external.supports: Modern thermal/carbonate experiments; short-contact cracking is attributed mainly to thermal shock. Does not establish a Khufu manufacturing history.
external.access: Publisher-indexed Methods, Results and Discussion; direct page retrieval redirected to an inaccessible identity endpoint

external.label: Reaction interfaces — Winter et al., 2005
external.citation: R. Winter et al., Tracing the reactive melting of glass-forming silicate batches by in situ 23Na NMR, DOI 10.1021/jp045705s
external.supports: Primary powder-batch NMR evidence for metasilicate formation and changing interface-controlled kinetics. Massive-rock scaling requires additional inputs.
external.access: Primary research abstract indexed in PubMed; publisher full text inaccessible

external.label: Aqueous quartz kinetics — Worley et al., 1996
external.citation: W. G. Worley, J. W. Tester and C. O. Grigsby, AIChE Journal 42, 3442–3457 (1996)
external.supports: Aqueous 100–200 °C quartz kinetics; apparent activation energy 72 ± 6 kJ/mol in the stated NaOH/NaCl regime. No molten-salt extrapolation.
external.access: Publisher abstract and indexed original paper at https://electronicsandbooks.com/edt/manual/Magazine/A/AIChE%20Journal%20US/1996%20v.42/12%20%283301-3570%29/3442-3457.pdf

external.label: Firesetting field evidence — Storemyr, 2014
external.citation: Per Storemyr, field-author account of Heldal et al., DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-09048-1_56
external.supports: Quarry-context observations and experiments provide thermal/mechanical comparators. Their site and date do not transfer automatically to Khufu.
external.access: Full author account; linked chapter not independently reanalysed

external.label: Natron composition — Raman study, 2007
external.citation: Raman spectroscopy of natron: shedding light on ancient Egyptian mummification (2007)
external.supports: Natural deposits contain carbonate, bicarbonate and chloride/sulfate impurities; composition must be specified rather than equated with a hydroxide reagent.

external.label: Carbonate formula mass — NIST WebBook
external.supports: Na₂CO₃ molecular weight 105.9884; reference for the rounded formula-mass arithmetic. Other formula masses are declared calculation constants.
